title: One in Four Teens Not Getting Enough Exercise
paragraphs: Regular exercise is important for young people's health, but a new global study suggests that many teenagers around the world are not getting nearly enough of it.

The study, which was published in the medical journal The Lancet Global Health, analyzed data from 389 surveys of 3.2 million adolescents aged between 11 and 17 in 140 countries. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), adolescents should do at least 60 minutes of moderate to vigorous physical activity, such as brisk walking or playing soccer, every day.

However, the study found that in 2025, about one in four adolescents worldwide, or around 240 million young people, did not reach this level of activity on a single day of the week. On average, adolescents were active on just 2.7 days a week, which was exactly the same as in 2010. Only 14% were active every day.

The study also found a clear gap between boys and girls. In virtually all countries, girls were less active than boys. On average, boys were active on three days a week, compared with 2.4 days for girls. Nearly 30% of girls did not reach the recommended level of activity on any day, compared with 22% of boys.

There were also big differences between regions. In wealthier regions, adolescents were active on about four days a week. In contrast, in lower- and middle-income regions, they were active on only about two days a week. Finland, Canada and Serbia were among the most active countries, while Cambodia, Jordan and Madagascar were among the least active.

The researchers believe that wealthier countries are better able to build safe places for young people to be active, such as open spaces and safe routes for walking and cycling. They called on governments to act faster, focusing especially on the least active teenagers and on removing the barriers that prevent girls from exercising.
